title: Pillars of Creation
subtitle: The Eagle Nebula, 6,500 light-years away
facts: This is Hubble's near-infrared view of the Eagle Nebula. Infrared light passes through much of the gas and dust, so the pillars become wispy silhouettes against a sky full of stars that were hidden before.
journeyIntro: These are towers of gas and dust, light-years tall. Stars are being born inside them. Move slowly here — the sound is meant to be a choir, not a machine.

hotspots.name: The tallest pillar
hotspots.text: The leftmost tower. It is a column of cold hydrogen, and at its tip the gas is collapsing into new stars. The sound is open and airy at the top and darker where the dust is thick.

hotspots.name: The middle tower
hotspots.text: The central column, edged in light. That bright rim is gas being evaporated by the radiation of nearby young stars — the pillars are being slowly eaten away.

hotspots.name: The star field
hotspots.text: In near-infrared the background is crowded with stars that the visible-light picture cannot see. Each tiny point is a sun. The sound here is a scatter of small bright accents.

hotspots.name: The blue haze
hotspots.text: A blue veil of scattered starlight between the towers. It is not fog and it is not smoke — it is light from thousands of stars, spread thin. The sound is soft and wide here, with almost no edge to it.
